observation.visible_scene: A light-haired person viewed from behind stands centered on a glossy stage floor strewn with scattered confetti/petal fragments (red and gold). They wear a black short-sleeved shirt and dark trousers, with a guitar slung across their back so the headstock/neck protrudes to the left and the body sits at the right hip. The background is filled with drifting haze/smoke lit by two bright spotlights, one upper-left and one upper-right, with a warm-toned wall visible at the far left edge.
visible_changes: At t=0 the arms are bent with hands held close to the torso; over the next several frames (t~0.08–0.5) the arms sweep outward and upward into a wide, raised V shape, hands opening toward the two lights.
During the early arm-raise there is a small weight shift / step in the legs (heels lifting and repositioning), after which the feet settle and remain roughly planted.
From about t=0.5 to the end (t=3.34) the outstretched raised-arm pose is largely held, with only minor adjustments in arm angle and hand position; the guitar neck stays fixed on the left throughout.
The background haze drifts and swirls slowly; the two spotlights remain in fixed screen positions; the confetti on the floor does not move.
No editing cut is apparent within the segment; the motion reads as continuous physical movement of the performer rather than a camera pan (the lights and figure stay centered).
outside_clip_unknowns: What the person does before t=0 and after the final frame (e.g., whether they turn, lower their arms, or begin playing) is not shown.
The cause or meaning of the raised-arm gesture and whether the segment is part of a performance or arrival is not established within the excerpt.
uncertain_details: Whether the early leg motion is a true step or only a weight/heel shift is hard to confirm from the sampled frames.
Any slight camera movement (push-in or drift) is uncertain given the static background cues; the framing appears essentially fixed.
The exact identity of the floor debris (confetti vs. petals) and the guitar type cannot be confirmed from the silhouette/back view.
